core_obligations: Prove (1): if each h_i : X_i \to Y has P for an \'etale covering, then for every |x| pick (i, x_i) over x, use the \'etale morphism of pairs (X_i, x_i) \to (X, x) and id_Y smooth as the diagram in part (3) of the definition to conclude f has P; conversely use part (1) of the definition (proof lines 3188-3199).

Prove (2): for a smooth covering {Y_i \to Y}, base change, use that X_i \to X \times_Y Y_i is an isomorphism hence \'etale and Y_i \to Y smooth to fit part (3) of the definition of smooth locality on the target, with the converse from its part (2) (proof lines 3201-3214).

Prove (3): for f with P and g : Y \to Z \'etale, use \'etale permanence for X \to Y \times_Z X (cited) and smoothness of Y \to Z to make the displayed square work for every x in part (3) of the definition, concluding g \circ f has P (proof lines 3216-3226).

Prove (4): from g \circ f has P get pr_Y : Y \times_Z X \to Y has P by part (2) of the definition; then (f, 1) : X \to Y \times_Z X is \'etale as a section of the \'etale projection (cited), and f = pr_Y \circ (f, 1) has P by part (1) (proof lines 3228-3235).
proof_roadmap: Unfold the two locality definitions along coverings and pair-morphisms.
Handle the target-smooth covering case via the isomorphism X_i \cong X \times_Y Y_i.
Build the \'etale/smooth squares for postcomposition and permanence, citing the two \'etale-permanence lemmas.
difficulty_reason: The author announces 'We write everything out completely' and proves all four parts in full: (1) uses that the \'etale morphism of pairs (X_i, x_i) \to (X, x) together with id_Y supplies the diagram demanded by part (3) of the \'etale-smooth locality definition, plus the converse from part (1) of the definition; (2) runs the analogous argument with smooth coverings of the target, using that X_i \to X \times_Y Y_i is an isomorphism hence \'etale; (3) builds the square with X \to Y \times_Z X \'etale (\'etale permanence, cited) and Y \to Z smooth, fitting part (3) of the definition for every x; (4) deduces f = pr_Y \circ (f, 1) with (f, 1) \'etale as a section of the \'etale projection (cited), then pr_Y has P by base change and f by part (1). Each part is a separate argument with its own diagram; the assembly is the substance.
